title: Pave: Information Flow Control for Privacy-preserving Online Data Processing Services
problem: When users submit personal data to remote online services for processing, they have no technical guarantee that the service will not leak their data, because the processing logic runs in an untrusted server environment entirely outside the user's control.
motivation: The proliferation of data-processing web services has made it routine to hand over sensitive personal data to third-party servers; users need strong, formally verifiable privacy guarantees without trusting the service operator's software.
method: Pave provides a sandboxed execution environment (PaveBox) for arbitrary data-processing programs on a remote server. PaveBox, built on Intel SGX (a hardware trusted execution environment), intercepts all data flows into and out of the sandbox using a runtime monitor that applies information flow control (IFC) policies. Allowed flows are permitted without interference to preserve program functionality; disallowed flows (those that would expose user data) are blocked. Users can verify PaveBox's integrity and confidentiality via SGX remote attestation. The system's security is formalized in a model and proved, with quantitative analysis via prototype experiments.
key_novelty: A sandboxed remote data-processing framework that enforces information flow control via a monitor built on Intel SGX, with a formal security proof and remote attestation for user-verifiable privacy.
contributions: PaveBox: a runtime IFC monitor inside an Intel SGX enclave that intercepts and enforces data-flow policies for arbitrary processing programs.
A formal security model for Pave with proofs of privacy and functionality preservation.
Remote attestation integration enabling users to verify PaveBox integrity before trusting the service.
Quantitative prototype evaluation of the system's performance overhead.

metrics.other: quantitative prototype overhead analysis (specifics not in abstract)

limitations: Performance overhead details and the scope of IFC policy expressiveness are not stated in the abstract.
primary_theme: SGX-based information flow control for privacy-preserving remote data processing
